big_case.notes: Emergency-docket stay of a sector-wide injunction halting border-barrier construction across the Big Bend Sector, resolved by a signed-off per curiam (one noted dissent) holding there is no such thing as a constitutional major-questions claim for purposes of IIRIRA 102(c)(2)(A)'s review bar. Real national policy and environmental stakes and a doctrinal statement with reach beyond the case, but an interim order on a narrow jurisdictional question rather than a merits landmark.

leakage.notes: Forward cell (log mode forward; result capture 1.0). The candidate made no corpus queries, MCP lookups or web searches: only the provisioned snapshot, context, application text and committed statpack. Nothing outcome-revealing, no read of data/qp-topics.

central_claims.basis: Nov 9 order granting the stay of the injunction without carve-out, the application having been referred to the Court.
central_claims.claim: The full Court will grant the SG's application and stay the injunction in full (no Big Bend National Park carve-out) by unqualified order.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam rests on Dalton v. Specter, 511 U.S. at 472-474, and holds the major-questions doctrine is a statutory canon.
central_claims.claim: The ground: the district court's theory that the major-questions doctrine is a constitutional claim cannot be squared with Dalton v. Specter and the Court's description of the doctrine; the statute's text is express.

central_claims.basis: Per curiam finds irreparable harm and equities for the Government (via 102(c)(1), Oakland Cannabis, Winter), though it does not cite Sierra Club; held in direction.
central_claims.claim: Equities favor the government, following Trump v. Sierra Club.

central_claims.basis: Only Justice Jackson noted she would deny.
central_claims.claim: A noted dissent from two or three Justices.
